ai.literal: Than poverty painful thing what if asked, like poverty poverty itself painful thing.
ai.translation: If asked what is more painful than poverty, poverty alone is as painful as poverty.
ai.modern: வறுமையை விடத் துன்பம் தருவது எது என்று கேட்டால், வறுமையைப் போலத் துன்பம் தருவது வறுமை மட்டுமே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the unparalleled suffering caused by poverty. The poet asks a rhetorical question: what is more painful than poverty? The answer is that nothing else compares to it; only poverty itself is as painful as poverty. The fifth case suffix 'இன்' (in) is used twice here, first to mean 'more than' and then to mean 'like'. The repetition of the words 'இன்மை' (poverty) and 'இன்னாதது' (painful thing) reinforces the absolute and unique nature of the misery it brings.

ai.literal: Poverty called a sinner, the next birth and this birth without, will come.
ai.translation: The wretch called poverty comes to deprive a person of the joys of both this world and the next.
ai.modern: வறுமை என்று சொல்லப்படும் பாவி, ஒருவனுக்கு இப்பிறப்பின் இன்பமும் மறுபிறப்பின் பயனும் இல்லாமல் செய்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet personifies poverty as a wretched sinner (paavi). It states that when poverty comes, it deprives a person of happiness in this current life (immai) and prevents them from doing good deeds that would secure a good life in the next (marumai). The word 'inri' (without) shows how poverty completely strips away the benefits of both states of existence.

ai.literal: Ancient lineage and honor and, will destroy altogether, poverty called craving.
ai.translation: The craving called poverty will completely destroy both one's ancient lineage and honor.
ai.modern: வறுமை என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஆசையானது, ஒருவருடைய பழமையான குடிப் பெருமையையும் அவருடைய மானத்தையும் ஒட்டுமொத்தமாக அழித்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet states that poverty is essentially a state of constant craving or desire. This relentless longing completely destroys a person's noble ancestry and their personal honor. The word 'தோல்' literally means skin, but here it is chosen to represent one's outward dignity or honor. The word 'நசை' highlights that poverty is fundamentally an affliction of unfulfilled desire. Together, poverty strips away everything that gives a person their social standing and self-respect.

ai.literal: noble family - those born - even among - poverty - disgraceful - word - that are born - weakness - will give
ai.translation: Poverty brings a weakness that gives rise to disgraceful words, even among those born in noble families.
ai.modern: நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்தவர்களிடத்திலும், வறுமையானது இழிவான சொற்கள் பிறப்பதற்குக் காரணமான சோர்வினை உண்டாக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how poverty can degrade even the most refined people. The word 'இல்' (il) here specifically means a noble or good family. 'இன்மை' (iṉmai), meaning poverty, is shown as a destructive force that brings 'சோர்வு' (cōrvu), a mental or moral weakness. Because of this weakness, even those raised with high standards may end up speaking 'இளிவந்த சொல்' (iḷivanda col), which are disgraceful or undignified words.

ai.literal: Within the affliction called poverty, many sorrows having gone will happen.
ai.translation: Within the single affliction called poverty, many other sorrows will come and gather.
ai.modern: வறுமை என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஒரு துன்பத்திற்குள், பல வகையான வேறு துன்பங்களும் தாமாகவே வந்து சேர்ந்து கொள்ளும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how poverty is not just a single hardship but a magnet for many others. The word 'நல்குரவு' means poverty, which is described as an 'இடும்பை' or affliction. Within this one affliction, 'பல்குரைத் துன்பங்கள்' (many kinds of sorrows) will go and occur. This shows that being poor brings about a multitude of secondary sufferings, such as hunger, humiliation, and loss of status.

ai.literal: Good meaning well having understood even if they say, the poor's words' meaning failing will suffer.
ai.translation: Even if the poor understand profound truths well and speak them, the meaning of their words will fail to carry weight.
ai.modern: நல்ல கருத்துகளைத் தெளிவாக உணர்ந்து சொன்னாலும், வறுமையுற்றவர்களின் சொற்கள் மற்றவர்களால் ஏற்கப்படாமல் வீணாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights how poverty undermines a person's voice in society. The phrase 'நற்பொருள் நன்குணர்ந்து சொல்லினும்' means that even if a poor person grasps good, profound ideas and articulates them well. 'நல்கூர்ந்தார் சொற்பொருள் சோர்வு படும்' concludes that the substance of their words will still fall flat or be ignored. The word 'சோர்வு' (failing or slipping) effectively captures how their wisdom loses its impact simply because of their impoverished state.

ai.literal: Virtue unassociated poverty, who-bore mother even, stranger like will-be-looked-at.
ai.translation: If a person suffers from poverty that is devoid of virtue, even the mother who bore him will look upon him as a stranger.
ai.modern: அறத்தோடு பொருந்தாத வறுமை ஒருவனை வாட்டினால், அவனைப் பெற்ற தாயும் அவனை ஒரு முன்பின் தெரியாத அயலானைப் போலவே பார்ப்பாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the extreme social alienation caused by severe, unvirtuous poverty. The phrase 'அறம் சாரா நல்குரவு' refers to a state of destitution that lacks any redeeming moral grace or prevents one from doing good. When a person falls into such a wretched state, the closest of all human bonds is broken. Even the mother who gave birth to him will distance herself and treat him like a complete stranger.

ai.literal: Even today coming-it indeed? even yesterday killed-it like poverty.
ai.translation: Will the poverty that almost killed me yesterday come again today?
ai.modern: நேற்றும் என்னைக் கொன்றது போலத் துன்புறுத்திய வறுமை, இன்றும் என்னிடம் வருமோ?
ai.explanation: The speaker personifies poverty as a deadly enemy. Having barely survived the agonizing hunger and suffering of yesterday, they dread the thought of facing it again today. The word 'கொன்றது' (killed) vividly captures the extreme pain of destitution, while 'கொல்லோ' expresses the speaker's deep anxiety and despair about the future.

ai.literal: Inside fire, even sleeping is possible; inside poverty, whatever even one (at all) sleep is difficult.
ai.translation: One might even be able to sleep in the midst of fire, but in the midst of poverty, sleep is utterly impossible.
ai.modern: நெருப்பின் நடுவே கூட ஒருவரால் தூங்கிவிட முடியும்; ஆனால் வறுமையின் பிடியில் சிக்கியிருக்கும்போது எந்த வகையிலும் தூங்குவது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses extreme hyperbole to contrast the physical pain of fire with the mental agony of poverty. The phrase 'நெருப்பினுள் துஞ்சலும் ஆகும்' suggests that a person might somehow find a way to sleep even while surrounded by flames. However, 'நிரப்பினுள் யாதொன்றும் கண்பாடு அரிது' emphasizes that in the grip of destitution, constant worry and suffering make it entirely impossible to close one's eyes in sleep. By comparing the two, the poet highlights that the torment of poverty is far worse than burning in a fire.

ai.literal: Means of subsistence those who lack completely not renouncing, to salt and to gruel is death.
ai.translation: When those who lack the means to live fail to renounce the world completely, they become a deadly burden even to the salt and gruel of others.
ai.modern: அடிப்படை வசதிகள் இல்லாதவர்கள் உலகத்தை முழுமையாகத் துறக்காமல் வாழ்வது, மற்றவர்களுடைய உப்புக்கும் கஞ்சிக்கும் எமனாக முடியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the severe burden of extreme poverty. The word 'tuppuravu' can mean enjoyment or purity, but here it specifically refers to the basic means of subsistence. When people utterly lack these means but still cling to worldly life, they must depend on others for the barest necessities. The poet uses the striking metaphor of 'kūṟṟu' (death or the destroyer) to show that such clinging consumes and destroys even the cheap salt and sour gruel of their neighbors.
